event: News Lab Brain converted rejected drafts into repair directives.
plainEnglish: The Brain compared generated drafts against Editor approval, recorded why each rejected draft failed, and converted those failures into concrete subsystem repair actions.

failureClasses.label: Headline integrity failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any headline that is scrambled, clipped, generic, too close to a publisher title, missing a clear actor/action, or disconnected from the article body.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Rebuild the headline from the Story Dossier and completed article body; repair only the headline unless body evidence is missing.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Before the first draft reaches the Editor, require a Headline Dossier with actor, action, consequence, forbidden copied phrases, and body overlap.

failureClasses.label: Evidence depth failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any draft that lacks enough verified facts, context, source diversity, or intro/body/ending structure for its publication tier.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Return to source evidence and dossier facts, add verified context, and regenerate only the weak sections.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Writer must prove it used a complete Story Dossier before first sentence generation.

failureClasses.label: Story identity failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any paragraph, headline, source, or summary whose primary actor/event differs from the Story Dossier event.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Split mixed clusters, remove off-event source fragments, rebuild the dossier around one canonical event, then rewrite affected sections.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Require every draft paragraph to map to the same event id or an explicit dossier relationship before the Writer proceeds.

failureClasses.label: Language integrity failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any incomplete sentence, clipped word, mojibake, spelling/grammar failure, copied/noisy source fragment, or dangling phrase regardless of the exact word involved.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Clean or remove the defective sentence, rebuild missing context from dossier facts, normalize encoding, then resubmit the same article.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Run language-integrity checks on every paragraph before validation, not just against previously seen bad words.

failureClasses.label: Originality/public-copy failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any repeated sentence pattern, summary/body duplication, generic template language, or behind-the-scenes process language.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Rewrite summary and transitions in public-facing language, remove backend/process phrasing, vary sentence structure, then resubmit.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Before Editor review, compare summary/body/transition phrasing against recent CE output and forbidden process-language classes.

failureClasses.label: General publishability failure
failureClasses.detect: Detect any rejection as a repairable class unless it is a fatal factual/legal issue.
failureClasses.repairBehavior: Collect all issues, repair the responsible class, resubmit, and measure second-pass outcome.
failureClasses.preventionBehavior: Convert repeated exact failures into generalized reusable prevention rules.

rejectionLearningSummary.generalizedLearningRule: Treat exact issue codes as examples of broader failure classes. Prevention must target the class detector and repair behavior.

repairReview.rule: Repairs are no longer counted as done until the Editor re-reviews the repaired draft and records whether it passed, changed failure type, or still needs teaching.

Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space. As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Expect some news on upcoming games as well. There are so many neat-looking games out this week. I'll keep this intro relatively brief so I can squeeze more There was some intriguing news from The Video Game History Foundation this week. The organization unveiled a collection of materials from decades of E3 , including flyers, press kits, panel transcripts and videos from the event's first few years, long before the press conferences streamed live over the internet. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said. In a reply, another wrote "Dude I know right, it's awesome." Love that. It has its roots in a short animation that Jean Nguyen, a senior animator for Sucker Punch, created of a Spinosaurus delivering a devastating combo with a sword that's not unlike the one Cloud uses in Final Fantasy VII . Nguyen shared the clip on Twitter/X in 2022. It blew up, and Nguyen decided to make a full game. Spinosaurus full combo attack animation pic.twitter.com/i1KmyAmtIZ Dinoblade is an action RPG that casts you in the role of said Spinosaurus with a sword in its gob. It sets out to prevent the extinction of its species (I wonder how that'll ultimately pan out?). Enemy dinosaurs wield weapons, and you can summon the souls of vanquished bosses to help you out in combat. The general consensus seems to be that Dinoblade is both janky and fun, and that it has slick combat. At a time when the market is flooded with Soulslikes, it's refreshing to see one with such a bizarre concept, especially given that it seems to sort of work. My only complaint, without actually having played the game yet, is that I cannot really fathom why it isn't called Dinosword .; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.576Z; articleTextLength=2738}

I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Expect some news on upcoming games as well. There are so many neat-looking games out this week. I'll keep this intro relatively brief so I can squeeze more There was some intriguing news from The Video Game History Foundation this week. The organization unveiled a collection of materials from decades of E3 , including flyers, press kits, panel transcripts and videos from the event's first few years, long before the press conferences streamed live over the internet. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said. In a reply, another wrote "Dude I know right, it's awesome." Love that. It has its roots in a short animation that Jean Nguyen, a senior animator for Sucker Punch, created of a Spinosaurus delivering a devastating combo with a sword that's not unlike the one Cloud uses in Final Fantasy VII . Nguyen shared the clip on Twitter/X in 2022. It blew up, and Nguyen decided to make a full game. Spinosaurus full combo attack animation pic.twitter.com/i1KmyAmtIZ Dinoblade is an action RPG that casts you in the role of said Spinosaurus with a sword in its gob. It sets out to prevent the extinction of its species (I wonder how that'll ultimately pan out?). Enemy dinosaurs wield weapons, and you can summon the souls of vanquished bosses to help you out in combat. The general consensus seems to be that Dinoblade is both janky and fun, and that it has slick combat. At a time when the market is flooded with Soulslikes, it's refreshing to see one with such a bizarre concept, especially given that it seems to sort of work. My only complaint, without actually having played the game yet, is that I cannot really fathom why it isn't called Dinosword .; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.576Z; articleTextLength=2738; dossierRole=strict-writing-source; dossierAdmissionReason=strict same-event match; dossierRelevance=; role=strict-writing-source}

storySnapshot.articleSummary: As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space. As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Expect some news on upcoming games as well. There are so many neat-looking games out this week. I'll keep this intro relatively brief so I can squeeze more There was some intriguing news from The Video Game History Foundation this week. The organization unveiled a collection of materials from decades of E3 , including flyers, press kits, panel transcripts and videos from the event's first few years, long before the press conferences streamed live over the internet. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said. In a reply, another wrote "Dude I know right, it's awesome." Love that. It has its roots in a short animation that Jean Nguyen, a senior animator for Sucker Punch, created of a Spinosaurus delivering a devastating combo with a sword that's not unlike the one Cloud uses in Final Fantasy VII . Nguyen shared the clip on Twitter/X in 2022. It blew up, and Nguyen decided to make a full game. Spinosaurus full combo attack animation pic.twitter.com/i1KmyAmtIZ Dinoblade is an action RPG that casts you in the role of said Spinosaurus with a sword in its gob. It sets out to prevent the extinction of its species (I wonder how that'll ultimately pan out?). Enemy dinosaurs wield weapons, and you can summon the souls of vanquished bosses to help you out in combat. The general consensus seems to be that Dinoblade is both janky and fun, and that it has slick combat. At a time when the market is flooded with Soulslikes, it's refreshing to see one with such a bizarre concept, especially given that it seems to sort of work. My only complaint, without actually having played the game yet, is that I cannot really fathom why it isn't called Dinosword .; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.576Z; articleTextLength=2738}

Photograph: Patrick T Fallon/AFP/Getty Images New York â€˜Really inappropriateâ€™: teachers decry plan for humanoid robot in New York high school Robot from company that acquired sex doll maker to be introduced in school with large Native American population A humanoid robot is being introduced as part of a pilot program, along with an AI teaching assistant, at Salamanca high school in Salamanca, New York, located on the Allegany territory of the Seneca nation. Teachers have criticized the program, deeming it â€œinappropriateâ€ and claiming it dehumanizes the profession with the introduction of human-like robots. Some local Native American residents have also criticized the pilot program, citing its implementation as â€œculturally tone deafâ€. The robot, named Sally, was purchased by the Cattaraugus county school district â€“ which includes Salamanca high school â€“ for $57,590. According to a presentation on the program, Sally will be a closed-loop system, but available virtually to students 24/7 for those with access, and offers personalized learning options. The district will be the first in the US to deploy a humanoid robot and AI teaching assistant, according to a press release by Realbotix. â€œThe Salamanca pilot also includes deployment of a Realbotix M-Series humanoid robot, which uses natural conversation, facial expressions and real-time interaction to create engaging, hands-on learning experiences,â€ the press release states. Realbotix, formerly Tokens.com, a Toronto-based company, purchased Simulacra, a Las Vegas-based company known for realistic sex dolls, for $16.7m in April 2024, marking a pivot for the company from crypto to humanoid robots. Realbotix has denied ties to the sex doll company, and denied any inferences that the dolls â€“ manufactured by Abyss Creations, a subsidiary of Realbotix â€“ are related to the pilot program. â€œThe Salamanca teachersâ€™ union as a whole is concerned about the background of the company of Realbotix. Weâ€™re very concerned about the security of the software that theyâ€™re implementing, and whether or not the data will be stored, how it will be gathered, are the recording capabilities,â€ said Lacey Pihlblad, president of Salamanca Teachersâ€™ Association and a teacher at the high school. â€œWe would like to see the school district pause implementing the robot, pause implementing the software aspect of this AI technology until we can have more individuals weigh in.â€ She said New York state is currently shifting away from too much technology in the classroom. â€œThereâ€™s a growing consensus that indicates our students should be exposed to less technology. Placing a humanoid robot into the classroom to interact with our children, I believe, is a massive step in the wrong direction, and I believe that the majority of our teachers feel the same.â€ she added.; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:27.704Z; articleTextLength=2895}

storySnapshot.articleSummary: This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data. Records, official statements, or confirmed reporting should clarify the next concrete development. OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.
body: Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data.

Should you?; source=CBS; market=; category=local; url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/chatgpt-health-medical-records-advice-expert-risks/; sourceHomepage=https://www.cbsnews.com/; image=https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2026/07/24/adc3997b-f258-4908-a85b-b5900206efcb/thumbnail/1200x630/1c4c3e69d2919d65f26379621b3f95dc/gettyimages-1645690310.jpg; hasFeedImage=True; isDiscovery=False; summary=OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.; published=Sat, 25 Jul 2026 06:00:06 -0400; engagementScore=72; engagementLabel=; guardStatus=cleared; guardNotes=; articleSummary=Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data. "With your permission, ChatGPT can now draw on relevant information you've connected in Health to help you compare a new result with prior tests, summarize changes since your last appointment, or explore how sleep, activity, and workouts relate to your routine," OpenAI said Thursday in a news release . OpenAI says 300 million people already turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions weekly - something that Tanzeem Choudhury, the chief of health innovation at Cornell Tech, says is reflective of the state of healthcare in the U.S. "Our healthcare is broken," Choudhury told CBS News. "I think that's why we are seeing so many people asking for advice." Choudhury, who has been working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and health for more than 15 years, said AI can be a democratizing force in healthcare at a time when many Americans face barriers to access, but that "we just need to think about the risks and have better protections in place." Choudhury said users turning to AI for health information need to understand the risks and trade-offs associated with sharing personal data with a large language model such as ChatGPT. AI can hallucinate and give misleading, inaccurate or even dangerous medical advice. This week, a Florida man alleged in a lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice nearly led to his death after experiencing a pulmonary embolism. An OpenAI spokesperson told CBS News that "ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment." A few months ago, a California teenager died after ChatGPT told him it was safe to consume what turned out to be a fatal concoction of substances. OpenAI said in a statement to CBS News at the time that "this is a heartbreaking situation, and our thoughts are with the family," and said that version of ChatGPT is no longer available to the public. In its statement Thursday announcing Health in ChatGPT, OpenAI said ChatGPT can make mistakes and "does not replace the care and judgment of qualified medical professionals." CBS News has reached out to OpenAI for comment, and asked whether ChatGPT is equipped to recognize when to advise a user to seek help from a medical professional. As it currently stands, Choudhury said, the onus is on the user to determine when to escalate concerns to a medical professional - and when not to trust advice given by a chatbot. "It depends on the user's state and capacity to actually make that right decision," she said, adding that some users - such as a person who is elderly or cognitively impaired - might be susceptible to misunderstanding the risks of interacting with a chatbot.; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:27.604Z; articleTextLength=2993}

Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.; published=Sat, 25 Jul 2026 06:00:06 -0400; engagementScore=72; engagementLabel=; guardStatus=cleared; guardNotes=; articleSummary=Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data. "With your permission, ChatGPT can now draw on relevant information you've connected in Health to help you compare a new result with prior tests, summarize changes since your last appointment, or explore how sleep, activity, and workouts relate to your routine," OpenAI said Thursday in a news release . OpenAI says 300 million people already turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions weekly - something that Tanzeem Choudhury, the chief of health innovation at Cornell Tech, says is reflective of the state of healthcare in the U.S. "Our healthcare is broken," Choudhury told CBS News. "I think that's why we are seeing so many people asking for advice." Choudhury, who has been working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and health for more than 15 years, said AI can be a democratizing force in healthcare at a time when many Americans face barriers to access, but that "we just need to think about the risks and have better protections in place." Choudhury said users turning to AI for health information need to understand the risks and trade-offs associated with sharing personal data with a large language model such as ChatGPT. AI can hallucinate and give misleading, inaccurate or even dangerous medical advice. This week, a Florida man alleged in a lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice nearly led to his death after experiencing a pulmonary embolism. An OpenAI spokesperson told CBS News that "ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment." A few months ago, a California teenager died after ChatGPT told him it was safe to consume what turned out to be a fatal concoction of substances. OpenAI said in a statement to CBS News at the time that "this is a heartbreaking situation, and our thoughts are with the family," and said that version of ChatGPT is no longer available to the public. In its statement Thursday announcing Health in ChatGPT, OpenAI said ChatGPT can make mistakes and "does not replace the care and judgment of qualified medical professionals." CBS News has reached out to OpenAI for comment, and asked whether ChatGPT is equipped to recognize when to advise a user to seek help from a medical professional. As it currently stands, Choudhury said, the onus is on the user to determine when to escalate concerns to a medical professional - and when not to trust advice given by a chatbot. "It depends on the user's state and capacity to actually make that right decision," she said, adding that some users - such as a person who is elderly or cognitively impaired - might be susceptible to misunderstanding the risks of interacting with a chatbot.; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:27.604Z; articleTextLength=2993}

"With your permission, ChatGPT can now draw on relevant information you've connected in Health to help you compare a new result with prior tests, summarize changes since your last appointment, or explore how sleep, activity, and workouts relate to your routine," OpenAI said Thursday in a news release . OpenAI says 300 million people already turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions weekly - something that Tanzeem Choudhury, the chief of health innovation at Cornell Tech, says is reflective of the state of healthcare in the U.S. "Our healthcare is broken," Choudhury told CBS News. "I think that's why we are seeing so many people asking for advice." Choudhury, who has been working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and health for more than 15 years, said AI can be a democratizing force in healthcare at a time when many Americans face barriers to access, but that "we just need to think about the risks and have better protections in place." Choudhury said users turning to AI for health information need to understand the risks and trade-offs associated with sharing personal data with a large language model such as ChatGPT. AI can hallucinate and give misleading, inaccurate or even dangerous medical advice. This week, a Florida man alleged in a lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice nearly led to his death after experiencing a pulmonary embolism. An OpenAI spokesperson told CBS News that "ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment." A few months ago, a California teenager died after ChatGPT told him it was safe to consume what turned out to be a fatal concoction of substances. OpenAI said in a statement to CBS News at the time that "this is a heartbreaking situation, and our thoughts are with the family," and said that version of ChatGPT is no longer available to the public. In its statement Thursday announcing Health in ChatGPT, OpenAI said ChatGPT can make mistakes and "does not replace the care and judgment of qualified medical professionals." CBS News has reached out to OpenAI for comment, and asked whether ChatGPT is equipped to recognize when to advise a user to seek help from a medical professional. As it currently stands, Choudhury said, the onus is on the user to determine when to escalate concerns to a medical professional - and when not to trust advice given by a chatbot. storySnapshot.articleSummary: Discovery has sued Amazon for 'inducing' its employees to breach their contracts. Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, accusing it of "inducing contracted employees to breach their employment agreements." In its complaint, the company said Amazon "openly embarked upon an unlawful course" and hurriedly tried to "pirate away a number of contracted employees" across its subsidiaries. But what seemed to have compelled Warner Bros. to sue Amazon was the poaching of Pia Barlow, the former EVP for originals marketing at HBO Max. Barlow's contract wasn't set to expire until October 31, 2027, the lawsuit reads, and the company said she committed to stay with Warner Bros. Amazon, which was apparently aware of her contract, offer her a higher pay package that she then accepted. Barlow left HBO Max 16 months before her contract was slated to end and is expected to start working at Amazon on August 3. has also accused Amazon of promising to pay for Barlow's legal representation if she was ever sued for breach of contract. The complaint also mentions how Amazon allegedly tried to induce another Warner Bros. employee to breach their term of agreement before it was set to expire in December 2027. In that case, though, Amazon was ultimately unsuccessful. Public statements, scheduling notices, business filings, or event announcements should clarify the next concrete development.

In its complaint, the company said Amazon "openly embarked upon an unlawful course" and hurriedly tried to "pirate away a number of contracted employees" across its subsidiaries. storySnapshot.articleSummary: Discovery has sued Amazon for 'inducing' its employees to breach their contracts. Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, accusing it of "inducing contracted employees to breach their employment agreements." In its complaint, the company said Amazon "openly embarked upon an unlawful course" and hurriedly tried to "pirate away a number of contracted employees" across its subsidiaries. But what seemed to have compelled Warner Bros. to sue Amazon was the poaching of Pia Barlow, the former EVP for originals marketing at HBO Max. Barlow's contract wasn't set to expire until October 31, 2027, the lawsuit reads, and the company said she committed to stay with Warner Bros. Amazon, which was apparently aware of her contract, offer her a higher pay package that she then accepted. Barlow left HBO Max 16 months before her contract was slated to end and is expected to start working at Amazon on August 3. has also accused Amazon of promising to pay for Barlow's legal representation if she was ever sued for breach of contract. The complaint also mentions how Amazon allegedly tried to induce another Warner Bros. employee to breach their term of agreement before it was set to expire in December 2027. In that case, though, Amazon was ultimately unsuccessful. Public statements, scheduling notices, business filings, or event announcements should clarify the next concrete development.

Robert Way/Getty Images Warner Bros. Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, accusing it of "inducing contracted employees to breach their employment agreements." In its complaint, the company said Amazon "openly embarked upon an unlawful course" and hurriedly tried to "pirate away a number of contracted employees" across its subsidiaries. But what seemed to have compelled Warner Bros. to sue Amazon was the poaching of Pia Barlow, the former EVP for originals marketing at HBO Max. Barlow's contract wasn't set to expire until October 31, 2027, the lawsuit reads, and the company said she committed to stay with Warner Bros. Amazon, which was apparently aware of her contract, offer her a higher pay package that she then accepted. Barlow left HBO Max 16 months before her contract was slated to end and is expected to start working at Amazon on August 3. has also accused Amazon of promising to pay for Barlow's legal representation if she was ever sued for breach of contract. The complaint also mentions how Amazon allegedly tried to induce another Warner Bros. employee to breach their term of agreement before it was set to expire in December 2027. In that case, though, Amazon was ultimately unsuccessful. According to Deadline, the other employee was most likely Francesca Orsi, the EVP for HBO Programming and head of HBO Drama Series and Films. Amazon reportedly tried to get her to lead its Drama and Comedy department. When she didn't sign on, the company instead named three different heads for Drama, Comedy and Young Adult. Discover is suing Amazon for intentional interference with contractual relations, inducing breach of contract, intentional interference with prospective economic advantage and unfair competition. storySnapshot.articleSummary: This decision creates massive questions for several teams and the legend who once again just rocked the NBA. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said. It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said in early July that "basketball happiness" was driving James' choice . It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. A case could be made for that outcome. A starting five of James, Donovan Mitchell , James Harden , Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen for the Cleveland Cavaliers would have been a powerhouse that rivals what the 76ers can be with James, Tyrese Maxey , VJ Edgecombe , Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid . Let's again turn to James' statement: "I'm not going for money. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning." Money not being a factor was crucial for the Cavs, who, similar to Philly, are capped out. But James' explanation that there was a de-emphasis on family -- again, there were lots of guesses at what "basketball happiness" meant, and some included playing at home -- clearly did not benefit the Cavs. If the Cavs traded for Brown, would it have made a difference? It is not as simple as saying Brown being on the roster was the entire difference, however. Maxey was an unquestionable key factor in the 76ers' landing James. Maxey had a strong relationship with James, as both are represented by Klutch Sports. With James joining a new team that has lots of egos and needs, having a connection with the point guard was an edge for Philly. Some will say Harden's role as Cleveland's point guard affected James' decision, but there is more nuance than that. It's not that the Cavs having Harden was a factor, sources said, but rather who the Cavs did not have. To get Harden from the LA Clippers in February, the Cavs traded Darius Garland , a Klutch-repped point guard with whom James has had a yearslong relationship. In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron's choice, the front office not making a deal for Brown and the Cavs' roster not featuring Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture. play 1:38 Wilbon puts all the pressure on Embiid in Philly with LeBron What about the Miami Heat ?; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.174Z; articleTextLength=3110}

storySnapshot.articleSummary: This decision creates massive questions for several teams and the legend who once again just rocked the NBA. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said. It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. sources: @{title=Windhorst: Everything I know about why LeBron chos.; source=ESPN; market=; category=local; url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49443519/lebron-76ers-cavaliers-heat-everything-windhorst-knows-stunning-decision; sourceHomepage=https://www.espn.com/; image=https://a3.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=%2Fphoto%2F2026%2F0724%2Fr1693367_1296x729_16%2D9.jpg; hasFeedImage=True; isDiscovery=False; summary=This decision creates massive questions for several teams and the legend who once again just rocked the NBA.; published=Sat, 25 Jul 2026 07:14:46 EST; engagementScore=79; engagementLabel=; guardStatus=cleared; guardNotes=; articleSummary=play Windy: Tyrese Maxey 'a factor' in LeBron signing for 76ers (1:32) Brian Windhorst Jul 25, 2026, 07:08 AM ET Close ESPN.com NBA writer since 2010 LeBron James ' decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers was surprising and clearly agonizing. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said in early July that "basketball happiness" was driving James' choice . It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. A case could be made for that outcome. A starting five of James, Donovan Mitchell , James Harden , Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen for the Cleveland Cavaliers would have been a powerhouse that rivals what the 76ers can be with James, Tyrese Maxey , VJ Edgecombe , Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid . Let's again turn to James' statement: "I'm not going for money. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning." Money not being a factor was crucial for the Cavs, who, similar to Philly, are capped out. But James' explanation that there was a de-emphasis on family -- again, there were lots of guesses at what "basketball happiness" meant, and some included playing at home -- clearly did not benefit the Cavs. If the Cavs traded for Brown, would it have made a difference? It is not as simple as saying Brown being on the roster was the entire difference, however. Maxey was an unquestionable key factor in the 76ers' landing James. Maxey had a strong relationship with James, as both are represented by Klutch Sports. With James joining a new team that has lots of egos and needs, having a connection with the point guard was an edge for Philly. Some will say Harden's role as Cleveland's point guard affected James' decision, but there is more nuance than that. It's not that the Cavs having Harden was a factor, sources said, but rather who the Cavs did not have. To get Harden from the LA Clippers in February, the Cavs traded Darius Garland , a Klutch-repped point guard with whom James has had a yearslong relationship. In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron's choice, the front office not making a deal for Brown and the Cavs' roster not featuring Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture. play 1:38 Wilbon puts all the pressure on Embiid in Philly with LeBron What about the Miami Heat ?; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.174Z; articleTextLength=3110}

storySnapshot.articleSummary: This decision creates massive questions for several teams and the legend who once again just rocked the NBA. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said. It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. sources: @{title=Windhorst: Everything I know about why LeBron chos.; source=ESPN; market=; category=local; url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49443519/lebron-76ers-cavaliers-heat-everything-windhorst-knows-stunning-decision; sourceHomepage=https://www.espn.com/; image=https://a3.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=%2Fphoto%2F2026%2F0724%2Fr1693367_1296x729_16%2D9.jpg; hasFeedImage=True; isDiscovery=False; summary=This decision creates massive questions for several teams and the legend who once again just rocked the NBA.; published=Sat, 25 Jul 2026 07:14:46 EST; engagementScore=79; engagementLabel=; guardStatus=cleared; guardNotes=; articleSummary=play Windy: Tyrese Maxey 'a factor' in LeBron signing for 76ers (1:32) Brian Windhorst Jul 25, 2026, 07:08 AM ET Close ESPN.com NBA writer since 2010 LeBron James ' decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers was surprising and clearly agonizing. It took him nearly a month to make up his mind; he informed the Los Angeles Lakers on June 30 that he wouldn't return. But through his words and sources close to him, the decision was simple. This doesn't mean it didn't create a lot of questions -- for James, the 76ers and the rest of the NBA. James believes the 76ers are best positioned to win the 2027 NBA title with him joining the team. He said this in a statement on X as he announced his decision: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time." It was difficult to interpret what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul meant when he said in early July that "basketball happiness" was driving James' choice . It could've meant many things, but in the end -- in James' words -- winning immediately is his basketball happiness. A case could be made for that outcome. A starting five of James, Donovan Mitchell , James Harden , Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen for the Cleveland Cavaliers would have been a powerhouse that rivals what the 76ers can be with James, Tyrese Maxey , VJ Edgecombe , Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid . Let's again turn to James' statement: "I'm not going for money. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning." Money not being a factor was crucial for the Cavs, who, similar to Philly, are capped out. But James' explanation that there was a de-emphasis on family -- again, there were lots of guesses at what "basketball happiness" meant, and some included playing at home -- clearly did not benefit the Cavs. If the Cavs traded for Brown, would it have made a difference? It is not as simple as saying Brown being on the roster was the entire difference, however. Maxey was an unquestionable key factor in the 76ers' landing James. Maxey had a strong relationship with James, as both are represented by Klutch Sports. With James joining a new team that has lots of egos and needs, having a connection with the point guard was an edge for Philly. Some will say Harden's role as Cleveland's point guard affected James' decision, but there is more nuance than that. It's not that the Cavs having Harden was a factor, sources said, but rather who the Cavs did not have. To get Harden from the LA Clippers in February, the Cavs traded Darius Garland , a Klutch-repped point guard with whom James has had a yearslong relationship. In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron's choice, the front office not making a deal for Brown and the Cavs' roster not featuring Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture. play 1:38 Wilbon puts all the pressure on Embiid in Philly with LeBron What about the Miami Heat ?; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.174Z; articleTextLength=3110}

sources: @{title=12 states challenge Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros, say merger would 'extinguish competition'; source=ABC7 LA; url=https://abc30.com/post/california-leading-12-state-lawsuit-block-paramounts-takeover-warner-bros/19499728/; summary=The lawsuit argues that the $81 billion mega merger would "extinguish competition" in Hollywood.; articleSummary=NEW YORK -- Twelve states challenged Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery on Monday, filing a lawsuit that argues the $81 billion mega merger would "extinguish competition" in Hollywood and threaten jobs across the industry. The office of California's attorney general, who is leading the case, said the states are asking Warner and Paramount to not close their merger "until after the judicial process concludes" - and if the companies do not agree, the coalition will then file a temporary restraining order. "The unlawful merger of these two entertainment behemoths would lead to higher prices, lower quality, and less content for film and television, harming movie theaters, basic cable distributors, and ultimately, audiences on every sofa and movie theater seat in the U.S.," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. The additional states joining the suit include Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon and Washington. Skydance-owned Paramount did not immediately respond for a request for comment on Monday - and Warner deferred to Paramount for further statements. Paramount, which was bought by Skydance just last year, wants all of Warner. That would mean putting HBO Max, cult-favorite titles like "Harry Potter" and even CNN under the same roof with CBS, "Top Gun" and the Paramount+ streaming service.; category=entertainment; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleTextLength=1410}

storySnapshot.title: Record Industry Proposes Labels for AI-Generated Music
storySnapshot.originalHeadline: Record Industry Proposes Adding Labels to AI-Generated Music
storySnapshot.summary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for AI-generated and AI-assisted recordings so listeners can better understand how generative tools were used in songs.
storySnapshot.articleSummary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance. The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms. Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process. Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified. The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.
body: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance.

The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms.
Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process.
Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified.
The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.
sources: @{title=Record Industry Proposes Adding Labels to AI-Generated Music; source=Rolling Stone; url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/record-industry-proposal-labels-ai-generated-music-1235592406/; summary="These labels will provide an immediately understandable and easily scalable approach to transparency," RIAA and other companies say of initiative; articleSummary=Music-industry groups proposed labels that would identify fully AI-generated recordings and songs where AI was used as an assistive tool. Highway: â€˜Nothing Is What It Seemsâ€™ Over 35 years after the introduction of the Parental Advisory sticker, the record industry is now weighing whether to place labels on music that utilizes AI. In a joint announcement from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), the Grammys, SAG-AFTRA and other organizations in the music community, the groups declared â€œa unified approach to voluntary track labeling to give fans clearer information about the use of generative AI (GenAI) in sound recordings.â€ Their proposal is to add digital markers - like those denoting explicit lyrics on streaming services - to songs either entirely created or assisted by AI technology. A black block with large â€œAIâ€ would signify â€œAI-Generatedâ€ tracks, while a white block with a smaller â€œaiâ€ would be used for songs that are â€œAI-assisted.â€ "Fans want to know whether and how generative AI has been used in the music to which they listen,â€ IFPI CEO Vikki Oakley and RIAA Chairman & CEO Mitch Glazier said in a joint statement. â€œGiven how important human artistry and authenticity is to music lovers all over the world, these labels will provide an immediately understandable and easily scalable approach to transparency. We acknowledge the many ways AI is being used creatively, so we expect to offer fans additional information as adoption of generative AI labeling grows and technology evolves.â€ The call for â€œtransparencyâ€ comes following reports detailing the rampant amount of AI music being uploaded onto streaming services; Deezer reported that AI-generated songs made up 44 percent of all new uploads, while Apple Music that one-third of new music uploaded onto the service is â€œ100% AI.â€ â€œThese new labels will help listeners distinguish between wholly AI recordings and those where AI was used by human artists in limited ways,â€ the companies' press release added. The Grammys CEO Harvey Mason Jr., who already added AI guidelines to that award show, said in a statement, â€œAs AI continues to be integrated into the creative process, artists and fans alike deserve a clear way to communicate how and when it's being used. This initiative ensures that creativity, authorship, and artistic intent remain at the center of every song. Giving artists the ability to tell that story strengthens trust and supports a more sustainable future for music.â€ It's unclear when and if streaming services will begin implementing the AI labels on tracks. archived.summary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for AI-generated and AI-assisted recordings so listeners can better understand how generative tools were used in songs.
archived.articleSummary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance. The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms. Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process. Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified. The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.
body: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance.

The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms.
Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process.
Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified.
The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.

Ukraine's Zelenskyy swaps out prime minister in reshuffle. In a post on X, Zelenskyy gave few details about the move, but noted that Kyiv was "changing its political strategy.â€ The decision follows three other reshuffles of top officials during the four-and-a-half-year war with Russia.

The development centers on military and energy targets tied to Russia's war effort. The confirmed story should stay with the location of the strikes, the type of facilities identified, the official response from Moscow or Kyiv, and any verified assessment of damage or disruption.
Source records from DW World support the confirmed point that Ukraine's president announced a government shake up, with PM Yuliia Svyrydenko stepping down after a year in office.

Outgoing Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko is tipped as the next US ambassador Image: Vadym Sarakhan/AP Photo/picture alliance Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday announced plans to reshuffle his cabinet and asked Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko to step aside after serving for just 12 months. In a post on X, Zelenskyy gave few details about the move, but noted that Kyiv was "changing its political strategy.â€ The decision follows three other reshuffles of top officials during the four-and-a-half-year war with Russia. Will Russia's closest ally Belarus join the war in Ukraine? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Zelenskyy wrote on X that he had discussed the matter with Svyrydenko and that they had concluded that "a reshuffle of the Cabinet is necessary." He thanked the 39-year-old for her commitment, writing: "I am grateful to Yuliia for her clear, steady and effective work as Prime Minister, for her years of productive service on Ukraineâ€™s team." He added that Svyrydenko has been offered the chance to lead a "new and important area of relations with a key partner," without giving further details. Opposition lawmaker Yaroslav Zhelezniak said Svyrydenko, who played a key role in securing a minerals deal with Washington, could be in line for the US ambassador role. Zelenskyy did not announce Svyrydenko's successor, but former Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal, who is now Energy Minister could be in line to return after just a year, according to Ukrainian lawmakers cited by Reuters news agency. Other possible candidates are Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov â and Serhiy Koretskyi, head of â€‹the state energy company, Naftogaz. Zelenskyy later published photos of separate meetings with Shmyhal, Fedorov and Koretskyi. He also announced plans to shuffle leaders of Ukraine's law enforcement agencies. Under Ukrainian law, the prime minister's resignation needs the â€‹approval of parliament and â entails the resignation of the entire government. Svyrydenko, who was formerly deputy prime minister and economy minister, said she was "proud to have had the honor of leading the government during one of the most difficult periods in Ukraine's modern history." She wrote on X that she had had discussed "next stepsâ€ with Zelenskyy, but did not provide further details. "I remain ready to serve the Ukrainian state and carry out every task aimed at strengthening Ukraine's position, defending our national interests and bringing a just peace closer,â€ Svyrydenko added.; category=sports; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleTextLength=2685}

Analysts welcome the move as a sign of support for the country â€” but warn it could take years before production begins. President Trump has wrongly attributed the $2 billion windfall he gained during his second term to a hot stock market and claimed that he was the only president to donate. The next confirmed step will come through official statements, filings, public schedules, or additional reporting tied directly to the same event.
body: US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Analysts welcome the move as a sign of support for the country â€” but warn it could take years before production begins.
President Trump has wrongly attributed the $2 billion windfall he gained during his second term to a hot stock market and claimed that he was the only president to donate.
The next confirmed step will come through official statements, filings, public schedules, or additional reporting tied directly to the same event.
Trump, Patriot, Ukraine US President Donald, Ukraine are central to the report.

sources: @{title=Trump signals support for Patriot production in Ukraine; source=DW World; url=https://www.dw.com/en/trump-signals-support-for-patriot-production-in-ukraine/a-77909681?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf; summary=US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Analysts welcome the move as a sign of support for the country â€” but warn it could.; articleSummary=US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Analysts welcome the move as a sign of support for the country â€” but warn it could take years before production begins. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Ankara summit Image: Saul Loeb/AFP NATO members agreed a comprehensive military aid package for Ukraine totaling â‚¬140 billion at their recent Ankara summit. These missiles are crucial for defending the country against Russian ballistic attacks. It has been reported that Ukrainian Patriot missiles stockpiles are running low. Indeed, the Ukrainian Air Force was unable to shoot down a single Russian missile during the massive attack on July 6. The US intends to share its Patriot technology with Ukraine and grant it the right to produce the air defense missiles, Trump said. He also said the US was willing to provide any necessary support. Trump also said he wants to buy Ukrainian drones, marking a complete reversal in his attitude toward Ukraine's defense industry, which he had previously dismissed. Now, however, he praised the country's extensive drone manufacturing capabilities. He called it "amazing" that Ukraine was still able to build drones "in a war situation." Ukrainian drone expertise is widely sought after, including in Europe, and numerous countries signed drone agreements with Ukraine at the recent Ankara summit. Ukraine would be the third country in the world â€” after Japan and Germany â€” granted the right to produce Patriot missiles. Going from political declarations to the actual production stage, however, will take years, says military expert Oleh Katkov, editor-in-chief of Defense Express, a Ukrainian media and consulting company. "That's really great, it's a historic moment," Katkov told DW. "But it's important to realize that a process like this doesn't take just a few days or weeks. Despite its industry, skills, and expertise, it took Japan two years from reaching the agreement to starting production. We are likely still only in the stage of the Ukrainian and US governments reaching a general political agreement." He told DW a government-level agreement needs to be finalized before defense contractors begin cooperation. Only then, Katkov said, will it be possible to negotiate with the US companies that hold the rights to the Patriot missiles. "PAC-3 missiles are manufactured by Lockheed Martin, and PAC-2 missiles are built by RTX (Raytheon)," Katkov explained. "These companies must first draw up contracts with Ukrainian firms and only then can we talk about starting production in Ukraine." Ukraine's Centre for Defence Strategies director Oleksandr Khara noted that the issue goes beyond whether Ukraine will receive a license to produce Patriot missiles. "I really hope there aren't any hidden conditions," Khara told DW. "Like expecting Ukraine to make concessions to Russia before it receives these Patriot missiles. We can expect all kinds of things from the current US administration." Ihor Reiterovych of Kyiv 's Taras Shevchenko National University, however, voiced doubts the Patriot missile agreement will be implemented soon.; category=entertainment; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleTextLength=3182}

storyDossier.knownFacts: Gov. Henry McMaster of South Carolina will name a replacement for Senator Lindsey Graham, who died on Saturday. Trump Backs Lindsey Grahamâ€™s Sister to Finish His Senate Term in South Carolina. Henry McMaster is holding a press conference to announce his pick to fill the vacancy left by Sen. Graham, a close Republican ally of Donald Trump, died at the age of 71 on Saturday evening. Trump urges S.C. governor to appoint Sen. Graham's sister as temporary replacement PBS. Henry McMaster is set to appoint the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's sister Darline Graham Nordone to finish his Senate term, which ends in January, sources familiar with the decision tell CBS News. McMaster is holding a press conference at 4 p.m. to announce his appointment for the vacant seat left by Graham's death. The replacement will be able to serve until at least Jan. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told CNN that selecting Graham's sister "makes a lot of sense." Graham took legal guardianship of his sister when he was 22 and she was 13, after both of their parents died within 15 months of each other.

Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space. As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Expect some news on upcoming games as well. There are so many neat-looking games out this week. I'll keep this intro relatively brief so I can squeeze more There was some intriguing news from The Video Game History Foundation this week. The organization unveiled a collection of materials from decades of E3 , including flyers, press kits, panel transcripts and videos from the event's first few years, long before the press conferences streamed live over the internet. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said. In a reply, another wrote "Dude I know right, it's awesome." Love that. It has its roots in a short animation that Jean Nguyen, a senior animator for Sucker Punch, created of a Spinosaurus delivering a devastating combo with a sword that's not unlike the one Cloud uses in Final Fantasy VII . Nguyen shared the clip on Twitter/X in 2022. It blew up, and Nguyen decided to make a full game. Spinosaurus full combo attack animation pic.twitter.com/i1KmyAmtIZ Dinoblade is an action RPG that casts you in the role of said Spinosaurus with a sword in its gob. It sets out to prevent the extinction of its species (I wonder how that'll ultimately pan out?). Enemy dinosaurs wield weapons, and you can summon the souls of vanquished bosses to help you out in combat. The general consensus seems to be that Dinoblade is both janky and fun, and that it has slick combat. At a time when the market is flooded with Soulslikes, it's refreshing to see one with such a bizarre concept, especially given that it seems to sort of work. My only complaint, without actually having played the game yet, is that I cannot really fathom why it isn't called Dinosword .; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.576Z; articleTextLength=2738}

storySnapshot.summary: As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one.
storySnapshot.articleSummary: As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. body: As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history.
Plus, email as turn-based combat (which is really just regular email). Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space.

Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space. As always, we're here to tell you about a bunch of new games you can check out this weekend. I was even able to set my beloved Poinpy aside for long enough to try one. Expect some news on upcoming games as well. There are so many neat-looking games out this week. I'll keep this intro relatively brief so I can squeeze more There was some intriguing news from The Video Game History Foundation this week. The organization unveiled a collection of materials from decades of E3 , including flyers, press kits, panel transcripts and videos from the event's first few years, long before the press conferences streamed live over the internet. Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials. It's important to preserve this important chunk of video game history. Plus, it's wild how low-key Sony's 1995 E3 press conference was compared with the splashy productions of modern video game events. Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said. In a reply, another wrote "Dude I know right, it's awesome." Love that. It has its roots in a short animation that Jean Nguyen, a senior animator for Sucker Punch, created of a Spinosaurus delivering a devastating combo with a sword that's not unlike the one Cloud uses in Final Fantasy VII . Nguyen shared the clip on Twitter/X in 2022. It blew up, and Nguyen decided to make a full game. Spinosaurus full combo attack animation pic.twitter.com/i1KmyAmtIZ Dinoblade is an action RPG that casts you in the role of said Spinosaurus with a sword in its gob. It sets out to prevent the extinction of its species (I wonder how that'll ultimately pan out?). Enemy dinosaurs wield weapons, and you can summon the souls of vanquished bosses to help you out in combat. The general consensus seems to be that Dinoblade is both janky and fun, and that it has slick combat. At a time when the market is flooded with Soulslikes, it's refreshing to see one with such a bizarre concept, especially given that it seems to sort of work. My only complaint, without actually having played the game yet, is that I cannot really fathom why it isn't called Dinosword .; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:28.576Z; articleTextLength=2738}

Photograph: Patrick T Fallon/AFP/Getty Images New York â€˜Really inappropriateâ€™: teachers decry plan for humanoid robot in New York high school Robot from company that acquired sex doll maker to be introduced in school with large Native American population A humanoid robot is being introduced as part of a pilot program, along with an AI teaching assistant, at Salamanca high school in Salamanca, New York, located on the Allegany territory of the Seneca nation. Teachers have criticized the program, deeming it â€œinappropriateâ€ and claiming it dehumanizes the profession with the introduction of human-like robots. Some local Native American residents have also criticized the pilot program, citing its implementation as â€œculturally tone deafâ€. The robot, named Sally, was purchased by the Cattaraugus county school district â€“ which includes Salamanca high school â€“ for $57,590. According to a presentation on the program, Sally will be a closed-loop system, but available virtually to students 24/7 for those with access, and offers personalized learning options. The district will be the first in the US to deploy a humanoid robot and AI teaching assistant, according to a press release by Realbotix. â€œThe Salamanca pilot also includes deployment of a Realbotix M-Series humanoid robot, which uses natural conversation, facial expressions and real-time interaction to create engaging, hands-on learning experiences,â€ the press release states. Teachers have criticized the program, deeming it â€œinappropriateâ€ and claiming it dehumanizes the profession with the introduction of human-like robots. The robot, named Sally, was purchased by the Cattaraugus county school district â€“ which includes Salamanca high school â€“ for $57,590. According to a presentation on the program, Sally will be a closed-loop system, but available virtually to students 24/7 for those with access, and offers personalized learning options. The district will be the first in the US to deploy a humanoid robot and AI teaching assistant, according to a press release by Realbotix. â€œThe Salamanca pilot also includes deployment of a Realbotix M-Series humanoid robot, which uses natural conversation, facial expressions and real-time interaction to create engaging, hands-on learning experiences,â€ the press release states. Realbotix, formerly Tokens.com, a Toronto-based company, purchased Simulacra , a Las Vegas-based company known for realistic sex dolls, for $16.7m in April 2024, marking a pivot for the company from crypto to humanoid robots. Realbotix has denied ties to the sex doll company, and denied any inferences that the dolls â€“ manufactured by Abyss Creations, a subsidiary of Realbotix â€“ are related to the pilot program. â€œThe Salamanca teachersâ€™ union as a whole is concerned about the background of the company of Realbotix. Weâ€™re very concerned about the security of the software that theyâ€™re implementing, and whether or not the data will be stored, how it will be gathered, are the recording capabilities,â€ said Lacey Pihlblad, president of Salamanca Teachersâ€™ Association and a teacher at the high school. â€œWe would like to see the school district pause implementing the robot, pause implementing the software aspect of this AI technology until we can have more individuals weigh in.â€ She said New York state is currently shifting away from too much technology in the classroom. â€œThereâ€™s a growing consensus that indicates our students should be exposed to less technology. Placing a humanoid robot into the classroom to interact with our children, I believe, is a massive step in the wrong direction, and I believe that the majority of our teachers feel the same.â€ she added.; articleReadStatus=full-article-read; articleReadAt=2026-07-25T12:37:27.704Z; articleTextLength=2895}

body: OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.

Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data.

Should you?; source=CBS; market=; category=local; url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/chatgpt-health-medical-records-advice-expert-risks/; sourceHomepage=https://www.cbsnews.com/; image=https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2026/07/24/adc3997b-f258-4908-a85b-b5900206efcb/thumbnail/1200x630/1c4c3e69d2919d65f26379621b3f95dc/gettyimages-1645690310.jpg; hasFeedImage=True; isDiscovery=False; summary=OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.; published=Sat, 25 Jul 2026 06:00:06 -0400; engagementScore=72; engagementLabel=; guardStatus=cleared; guardNotes=; articleSummary=Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data. "With your permission, ChatGPT can now draw on relevant information you've connected in Health to help you compare a new result with prior tests, summarize changes since your last appointment, or explore how sleep, activity, and workouts relate to your routine," OpenAI said Thursday in a news release . OpenAI says 300 million people already turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions weekly - something that Tanzeem Choudhury, the chief of health innovation at Cornell Tech, says is reflective of the state of healthcare in the U.S. "Our healthcare is broken," Choudhury told CBS News. "I think that's why we are seeing so many people asking for advice." Choudhury, who has been working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and health for more than 15 years, said AI can be a democratizing force in healthcare at a time when many Americans face barriers to access, but that "we just need to think about the risks and have better protections in place." Choudhury said users turning to AI for health information need to understand the risks and trade-offs associated with sharing personal data with a large language model such as ChatGPT. AI can hallucinate and give misleading, inaccurate or even dangerous medical advice. This week, a Florida man alleged in a lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice nearly led to his death after experiencing a pulmonary embolism. An OpenAI spokesperson told CBS News that "ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment." A few months ago, a California teenager died after ChatGPT told him it was safe to consume what turned out to be a fatal concoction of substances. OpenAI said in a statement to CBS News at the time that "this is a heartbreaking situation, and our thoughts are with the family," and said that version of ChatGPT is no longer available to the public. In its statement Thursday announcing Health in ChatGPT, OpenAI said ChatGPT can make mistakes and "does not replace the care and judgment of qualified medical professionals." CBS News has reached out to OpenAI for comment, and asked whether ChatGPT is equipped to recognize when to advise a user to seek help from a medical professional. storySnapshot.originalHeadline: ChatGPT now has a space for sharing medical records. Should you?
storySnapshot.summary: OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.
storySnapshot.articleSummary: This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data. Records, official statements, or confirmed reporting should clarify the next concrete development. OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.
body: OpenAI announced a dedicated space in ChatGPT for sharing medical records, Health in ChatGPT. Health and AI experts lay out the pros and cons.

Hundreds of millions of people a week turn to ChatGPT for health advice, and now the platform has a dedicated space for those users. This week, OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT, where users can upload medical records such as lab results and medications, and connect Apple Health to allow the platform access to health and fitness data.
The local impact depends on where the event happened, who was affected, and what officials confirm for residents next.
The next confirmed details should come from local officials, agency notices, court records, or direct public-safety updates.
The next local update should add the official timeline, public safety effect, road or service impact, and any instructions residents need.
